steps.text: Construct explicit separating examples such as A_5 and S_3 for the hierarchy.
Split into cases for A_5: the commutator subgroup is either trivial or all of A_5.
Invoke the class equation and orbit-stabilizer to write |G| as |Z(G)| plus non-central conjugacy classes.
Count over the conjugacy-class decomposition: every non-central class has size divisible by p, so |Z(G)| is divisible by p.
Since p divides |Z(G)|, bound it below by p and conclude the center is nontrivial.
Build the upper central series Z_i with Z_{i+1}/Z_i equal to the center of G/Z_i.
Use induction and well-ordering on the finite p-group order: the strictly increasing central series terminates at G.
